storyPrompt: Write a quiet English story about checking a disputed delivery before a public demonstration. Ivo is a practical conservator. Hana is an assistant who is allowed to disagree. Ben keeps the public records. The story takes place at the ferry office. The chart tube must remain intact. No character may be physically injured. Keep practical actions precise. Use third-person past tense centred on Ivo. Plan six chapters, each targeting 750 words. No earlier book or borrowed fictional world is assumed.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.purpose: Ivo receives the sealed chart tube and checks its outer label.
chapters.turn: Ivo notices a red seam but leaves it unopened.
hookSeeds: Who removed the second page of the crossing record?

chapters.title: Comparison
chapters.purpose: Ivo and Hana compare the label with the crossing record.
chapters.turn: They establish that the second page is absent and defer opening the chart tube.

chapters.title: The Duplicate
chapters.purpose: Ivo reads the handling note and asks Ben about the missing page.
chapters.turn: Ben supplies a duplicate page; the team agrees to continue checking before a demonstration.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.purpose: Ivo compares the duplicate with a pencil copy.
chapters.turn: Hana identifies a transposed line and they agree on a corrected label.

chapters.title: Demonstration
chapters.purpose: The team prepares the public demonstration at the ferry office.
chapters.turn: Ivo credits Hana for finding the error, without claiming the item was lost.

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.purpose: Ivo completes the demonstration and files the corrected crossing record.
chapters.turn: The intact chart tube is stored securely and the dispute is closed.

texts:
Ivo received the sealed chart tube and checked its outer label. The ferry office was open, though there were no visitors at the table. Ivo cleared a space before setting anything down. Hana moved the loose tools to a tray and waited for instructions. Neither of them treated a late delivery as proof of a lost object. They checked what they could see and left a blank beside what they could not yet establish.

The work required a little patience. A faded number was difficult to distinguish from a stain, so Ivo turned the sheet towards the window rather than writing over it. Hana read the number aloud. They compared their readings, found that they agreed, and entered it only once. The chart tube remained intact on the cleared table throughout the check.

Ivo made a short note of the work completed that day. The note separated observation from intention: a task written for tomorrow did not become a task already done. Hana asked whether the uncertainty meant they should abandon the demonstration. Ivo said that an unanswered question was a reason to check, rather than a reason to invent an answer. It was an ordinary distinction, but making it aloud helped them continue without blaming anyone.

Ivo noticed a red seam but left it unopened. They put the tools back in the tray. Ivo recorded that result and closed the current work period. The next planned task remained unwritten in the story. No one had opened a different room, visited another site, or completed the later demonstration in the interval between these actions.
